part1_current_maturity.score_rationale: A 62/100 reflects the paradox: infrastructure and governance are mature (~90), certification rate is high (90.5%), but cognitive calibration is severely broken (~25-30). Weighted: (90×0.35 infrastructure) + (80×0.25 certification/gov) + (25×0.40 cognitive) = 31.5 + 20 + 10 = 61.5 ≈ 62.

content_maturity.rationale: Cannot call content 'exam-ready' when 96.7% of items test only Understand/Apply and 0 items test Evaluate. The pool does not simulate actual CMA cognitive demands even at Part 1 level. The CAQS §6.1-6.2 targets (25% Difficult, 10% Very Difficult, 25% Analyze, 15% Evaluate) are not met for a single dimension. The blueprint item-count balance is the only dimension that passes — topic coverage, cognitive distribution, and difficulty calibration all fail. Content maturity must reach ~80/100 (via S831-S833 remediation) before Part 2 expansion can be credibly discussed.

infrastructure_readiness.rationale: Framework v2 adopted (97/100). Governance guard active (32/32 PASS with 6 rules). Validation suite functional (ExplanationValidator, identity validator). Batch enforcement via Rule 5 (≤30 items). Backup protocol enforced. REVISION_HISTORY.md protocol mature with 200+ entries. All infrastructure pieces needed for Part 2 exist — the certification pipeline, governance guard, backup protocol, and identity validator would scale to Part 2 with zero architectural changes. Loss of 2 points for manual certification pipeline (no CI/CD automation).

governance_readiness.rationale: 32/32 governance guard PASS across 6 rules. Rule 2 (DL-008 BLOCK), Rule 3 (registry protection), Rule 5 (30-item batch), Rule 6 (DL-026 BLOCK, added S814). Batch enforcement operational. Defect library with 36 entries (DL-001 through DL-036). REVISION_HISTORY.md protocol with documented before/after counts. Dual-verification cross-check mandate (AGENTS.md §5). Co-session governance (T0/Tmid/Tend checkpoints, AGENTS.md §13). The governance framework scales to Part 2 with zero changes — same rules, same guards, same protocols. Loss of 5 points because governance depends on per-item manual verification (not automated) and the certification pipeline has no built-in difficulty/Bloom's distribution enforcement.

pipeline_readiness.rationale: Certification pipeline operates at ~77 items per wave (S853 demonstrated). Six-dimension verification per CAQS §1.6 is standardized. However, the pipeline is manual — no automated content authoring, no continuous integration, no automated distribution checks. The DL-031 gap (800-1,000 items needing recalibration) would take 20-25 batches at 30 items/batch — 6-8 sessions. The Part 2 expansion would require authoring 800-1,200 new items, which at current pipeline throughput means 40-60 additional sessions. The pipeline works but does not scale to the throughput Part 2 demands without process optimization.

content_authoring_readiness.rationale: No established content authoring pipeline for new items. The existing 2,540 items came from template-rotation bulk generation — which caused the DL-012/013/031/032 problems. The 5-item rotation template produced broad but shallow coverage, mechanically-assigned difficulty labels with zero cognitive calibration, and definition-recognition stems that test at Understand, not Apply. Part 2 content would need a quality-first authoring process that produces items with genuine cognitive calibration from authoring time. This process does not exist. Agent F's VDiff item specification (multi-concept integration, 3+ exhibits, professional judgment, ambiguous fact patterns, mini-lesson explanations) is a design document, not an operational pipeline. Until the pipeline demonstrates it can produce 50 items at Analyze/Evaluate that pass 6-dimension verification at HIGH confidence, the project is not ready for Part 2 content creation.

expansion_readiness_verdict: NOT READY FOR PART 2. Part 1 content maturity must reach at least 80/100 before considering Part 2 expansion. The infrastructure and governance are ready — the content authoring process is not, and the Part 1 pool itself needs ~500-800 new items + ~800 recalibrations to become genuinely 'exam-ready.'

verdict_elaboration.why_infrastructure_is_not_enough: Having a certification pipeline, governance guard, and validation suite does not mean the project can author content at Part 2 quality. The Part 1 experience demonstrates that infrastructure quality does not guarantee content quality. All 2,540 Part 1 items passed validation, were parsed by the identity validator, and operated within governance guard rules — yet 96.7% test at Understand/Apply and 0 test at Evaluate. This was not a governance failure — the governance guard never had a rule for cognitive distribution. It was a content authoring failure: the template pipeline could not produce Analyze/Evaluate items no matter how many validation passes it underwent.
verdict_elaboration.why_content_authoring_readiness_is_the_g: The gap between Part 1's current state (0 Evaluate, 0.4% Analyze, 0% VDiff) and a genuine 'exam-ready' pool (15% Evaluate, 25% Analyze, 10% VDiff) requires ~750-1,000 new items at upper cognitive tiers. That is the equivalent of authoring an entirely new pack at quality levels the current pipeline has never demonstrated. Until the project successfully authors 50-75 Analyze/Evaluate items for Part 1 that pass 6-dimension verification at HIGH confidence, there is zero basis to believe it can author 800+ Part 2 items at equivalent quality.
verdict_elaboration.why_part_2_now_would_be_premature: Starting Part 2 content creation before fixing Part 1's cognitive distribution would compound the existing problem. Part 2 items would be authored through the same pipeline (or a new, untested one) and face the same calibration issues. The project would end up with two pools — both structurally deficient in upper-tier cognitive demand — rather than one mature pool and one that was built from learned quality-first authoring practices.

recommended_path.phase_1: Complete Part 1 cognitive maturity (S833 Sprints 1-4, ~300 hours — see S832_AGENT_D_EXPANSION_RANKING.json §execution_sequence_recommendation)
phase_1_milestones: Wave 1: DL-021 (95 items) + DL-016 (58 items) + Moderate→Difficult recalibration (423 items) = ~576 items, immediate learner impact
Wave 2: DL-031 coordinated sweep (~800-1000 items, paired with upward recalibration per S831 Agent G), Section F certification (124 items), VDiff bridge (22 items per S831 Agent F)
Wave 3: New VDiff items (50 in Sections B/C) + new Evaluate items (75 across all sections) — first test of quality-first authoring pipeline
Wave 4: Topic gap fills (60 items), case certification sweep (300 items)
phase_1_success_criteria: Difficulty distribution within 5pp of CAQS §6.1 targets on all 5 bands
Bloom's distribution: ≥10% Analyze, ≥5% Evaluate (intermediate targets, from 0.4%/0%)
≥200 Difficult items (up from 85), ≥20 Very Difficult items (up from 0)
0 DL-021, 0 DL-016, 0 DL-008 in learner pool
Content authoring pipeline demonstrated: 75 Evaluate + 50 VDiff items authored and certified
recommended_path.phase_2_description: Author 50-75 Analyze/Evaluate items using the Agent F specification (multi-concept integration, multi-exhibit dependency, professional judgment, plausible distractors). Document the process — from topic selection → stem authoring → distractor engineering → explanation writing → 6-dimension verification. This pipeline must demonstrate it can produce CAL-1/CAL-2/CAL-3 items at HIGH confidence before scaling to Part 2 production volumes. The pipeline itself is the deliverable — the 50-75 items are the proof.
recommended_path.phase_3: Begin Part 2 blueprint analysis and content specification
recommended_path.phase_3_description: Map the IMA CMA Part 2 Content Specification Outline to the existing governance/certification/infrastructure. Identify per-section item counts, topic allocation, cognitive distribution targets. Design the item template (50-75 items) for Part 2 using the validated pipeline from Phase 2. Produce a Part 2 content specification document equivalent to CAQS but scoped to Part 2 topics (financial statement analysis, corporate finance, decision analysis, risk management, investment decisions, professional ethics).
recommended_path.phase_4: Part 2 content creation using validated pipeline
recommended_path.phase_4_description: Author Part 2 items at Part 1-mature quality standards. Estimated: 800-1,200 items across equivalent of 6 domains. ~6-8 months of active authoring at 50 items/week using validated pipeline. Certification in waves of ≤200 items per the governance guard batch protocol. The pipeline established in Phase 2 eliminates the DL-012/013/031/032 recurrence risk — every item is authored at calibrated difficulty and Bloom's from creation, not retroactively adjusted.

risk_1_starting_part_2_now.description: Authoring 800+ Part 2 items through a pipeline that has never produced a single Evaluate item would guarantee the Part 2 pool inherits the same cognitive distribution defects as Part 1. The project would spend months producing a structurally identical pool — 90% Understand/Apply, 0% Evaluate — that fails to prepare candidates for the CMA Part 2 exam just as Part 1 currently fails.
risk_1_starting_part_2_now.probability: NEAR CERTAIN (based on Part 1 pipeline track record)
risk_1_starting_part_2_now.mitigation: DO NOT begin Part 2 content creation until Phase 2 pipeline validation succeeds.

risk_2_content_authoring_timeline.description: The Phase 1 remediation program (~300 hours, ~3,300 operations) plus Phase 2 pipeline development plus Phase 3 blueprint analysis could take 3-6 months. Stakeholders expecting a completed Part 1+2 simulator by Q4 2026 will be disappointed by this timeline.
risk_2_content_authoring_timeline.mitigation: Communicate the 'quality-first' philosophy early. A broken Part 2 pool is worse than no Part 2 pool. Phase 1 improvements alone (Waves 1-2) create immediate learner value on Part 1 while Part 2 planning proceeds.

risk_3_authoring_pipeline_may_fail.description: The project has never successfully authored a batch of Evaluate items. The Agent F specification is detailed but untested. It is possible that Evaluate-level distractor engineering is beyond current project capability — and discovering this after 3 months of attempting it would block all downstream phases.
risk_3_authoring_pipeline_may_fail.mitigation: Phase 2 is intentionally scoped small (50-75 items) as a pipeline proof-of-concept. If Evaluate authoring proves infeasible, the project pivots to maximizing Part 1 depth rather than expanding to Part 2.

risk_4_governance_guard_coverage_gap.description: The governance guard has no rule enforcing difficulty distribution or Bloom's distribution. S853 demonstrated this: 39 Domain F items were certified without checking DL-026 (DL-035). After S814 Rule 6 was added, DL-026 is blocked — but there is still no governance rule that blocks certification of items with DifficultyScore=3 when the stem is a textbook definition (DL-031). The certification pipeline can still produce pools with broken cognitive distributions.
risk_4_governance_guard_coverage_gap.mitigation: Add Rule 7 to governance guard: BLOCK certification when the item's stem-correct-choice Jaccard similarity exceeds threshold AND the DifficultyScore ≥ 3 (DL-031 enforcement). Also: add rule for Difficulty label ↔ DifficultyScore consistency (36.8% mismatch rate found by Agent F on Domain E).

disclaimer: This assessment is based on the S831-S833 discovery reports (2026-07-27). All counts are cross-verified against raw file grep evidence. The recommended path reflects the consensus of S831-S833 agents. The verdict 'NOT READY FOR PART 2' is not a judgment on project quality — it is an assessment of sequencing priority. Part 1 is structurally sound but cognitively incomplete. Complete Part 1 first, then build Part 2 with the validated pipeline. Infrastructure is ready; content authoring process is not.
